items.title: Willie Foster Interview
items.q: And I played with Joe Oliver. He had the Magnolia Band. Pops was playing bass.

ctx.x: Yes, both of those are dead. Thomas Batten. So I left out of there. I went with playing dance music, you know, with the other bands out in town. And the original Tuxedo Band, there's four of us made up that band. Ernest Trepania, the drummer. William Risley and myself. And Oscar Salisant. Right at my porch, we had four pieces organized, the original Tuxedo Band. So I played with the Tuxedo for a good while. And the band that split up. Salisant had a Tuxedo. And Risley had the Tuxedo Band. Each one, they had two.…
If you can remember, it'll be fine.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: We had three pieces, me and my brother and sister.

ctx.x: Permit. Had you played in any band or anything? Did you play in any band or up there in Assumption Barrett before you came down?

We had three pieces, me and my brother and sister. See, because remember my sister played manly. My sister played manly, my brother played guitar and I played cello. Did your father and your mother play anything? No, my father and my uncle, my father and my brother, he was a little ham fat violin player. And we used to play those, you used to give those warm, see they used to give a dance, they call them balls. They get one big room man and give a dance, 25 cents to come in, see. 15 cents every bite, take it…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Louis Kepp. And the leader? My brother.

ctx.x: Louis Kepp. And the leader? My brother.
Why did your brother play? Violin. What's his first name? Willie. Willie. Willie Foster. Yeah. I had Eddie Atkins. First we had Eddie Atkins.
